topics.content:
HTML Fundamentals — Complete Notes ________________ 1. What is HTML? 📖 Definition HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language used to create and structure content on web pages. HTML tells the browser what different pieces of content are. For example: * Heading →

* Paragraph →

* Image → * Link → * Button → CSS button { background-color: blue; color: white; } JavaScript button.addEventListener("click", function () { alert("Button clicked!"); }); Remember HTML → What is on the page? CSS → How does it look? JavaScript → How does it behave? ________________ 3. History of HTML HTML was created by Tim Berners-Lee while working at CERN. The purpose was to make it possible to connect and share documents using hyperlinks. Major HTML Milestones Version Important development HTML 1.0 Early foundation of HTML HTML 2.0 Standardization of HTML HTML 3.2 Added more presentation-related features HTML 4.01 Major widely used HTML standard XHTML HTML reformulated using XML rules HTML5 Modern HTML standard with multimedia and semantic features HTML5 introduced/improved features such as: * Semantic elements * Audio * Video * Canvas * SVG support * Better forms * Responsive-related capabilities * Web APIs 🔑 Important Point Modern HTML is maintained as a living standard rather than being treated as a completely frozen version. ________________ 4. HTML5 📖 Definition HTML5 refers to the modern generation of HTML that introduced many semantic, multimedia, form, and web-platform features. Example HTML5 Page

3. Links & Navigation in HTML 3.1 Introduction to Links Links allow users to move from one webpage or resource to another. HTML uses the (anchor) element to create links. Syntax Link Text Example Visit Google Here: * → anchor element * href → destination of the link * Visit Google → clickable text ________________ 3.2 The href Attribute The href attribute specifies the destination of a link. Example Visit Example Without href, an element does not have a normal link destination. Different Destinations About External Website Contact ________________ 3.3 Absolute URLs An absolute URL contains the complete web address. Example Google Other examples: GitHub YouTube Use Absolute URLs are commonly used when linking to external websites. ________________ 3.4 Relative URLs A relative URL points to a resource relative to the current webpage or document location. Suppose your project is: website/ │ ├── index.html ├── about.html ├── contact.html │ └── pages/ └── services.html From index.html: About To open services.html: Services Going Up One Directory From: pages/services.html to: index.html you can use: Home .. means the parent directory. ________________ 3.5 Linking to Another HTML Page Suppose you have: index.html about.html contact.html index.html

Home Page

About Us Contact Us about.html

About Page

Home This creates navigation between pages. ________________ 3.6 target Attribute The target attribute specifies where the linked document should open. _self Opens the link in the current browsing context. About This is the normal default behavior. _blank Opens the link in a new browsing context, usually a new browser tab. Visit Website _parent Opens the linked document in the parent browsing context. Open Page This is mainly relevant when working with nested browsing contexts such as iframes. _top Opens the linked document in the top-level browsing context. Open Page This is also mainly relevant when working with frames or iframes. ________________ 3.7 target="_blank" and rel When opening an external page with _blank, you may use: Visit Website noopener Prevents the newly opened page from accessing the opener through window.opener. noreferrer Requests that the browser not send the referring page URL in the Referer header and also implies noopener in modern browsers. Example Example ________________ 3.8 Email Links The mailto: scheme can be used to create an email link. Syntax Send Email Example Email Me Clicking the link normally opens the user's configured email application. ________________ 3.9 Telephone Links The tel: scheme can create a link for a telephone number. Example Call Us On compatible devices, this can open the phone/dialing interface. ________________ 3.10 SMS Links The sms: scheme can be used to create an SMS link on supported devices. Send SMS ________________ 3.11 Download Links The download attribute suggests that the linked resource should be downloaded instead of navigated to. Example Download Notes Custom Filename You can provide a suggested filename: Download HTML Notes Important Point The browser and server may affect whether the resource is downloaded and how the filename is handled. ________________ 3.12 Linking to a Specific Section of the Same Page You can create internal page navigation using an element's id. Step 1 — Add an id

HTML Basics

Step 2 — Link to the id Go to HTML Basics Clicking the link moves the user to that section. ________________ 3.13 Fragment Identifiers The # symbol is used to reference an element's id. Contact

Contact Us

Here: #contact is called a URL fragment. ________________ 3.14 Linking to a Section on Another Page You can also link directly to an element on another HTML page. about.html

Our Team

index.html Meet Our Team The browser opens about.html and navigates to the element with id="team". ________________ 3.15 Navigation Menu The
element is used for a section containing navigation links. Example
Home About Services Contact
Important Point
is semantic HTML. It tells browsers and assistive technologies that the section contains navigation links. ________________ 3.16 Navigation with Lists Navigation links are often organized using lists.
  • Home
  • About
  • Services
  • Contact
CSS can later be used to make these links appear horizontally. ________________ 3.17 Linking Images An image can be placed inside an anchor to make the image clickable. Clicking the image opens the linked destination. ________________ 3.18 Opening an External Website Visit GitHub This is useful when you want the user to visit another website without leaving the current page. ________________ 3.19 title Attribute on Links The title attribute can provide additional advisory information. About Us The browser may display the title as a tooltip. Important Point Do not rely on title as the only way to communicate important information. ________________ 3.20 download vs Normal Link Normal link Open PDF The browser may open the PDF. Download link Download PDF The browser is asked to download the resource. ________________ 3.21 Link to a PDF View HTML Notes Or: Download HTML Notes ________________ 3.22 Link to an Image View Photo ________________ 3.23 Link to a File in a Folder Suppose: website/ │ ├── index.html ├── notes/ │ └── html.pdf └── images/ └── logo.png From index.html: HTML Notes View Logo ________________ 3.24 Link to Parent Directory Suppose: website/ │ ├── index.html └── pages/ └── about.html Inside about.html: Home ../ moves one directory level upward. ________________ 3.25 Link to the Root of a Website A root-relative URL starts with /. About This refers to about.html relative to the website's root. ________________ 3.26 External vs Internal Links Type Example Purpose External https://example.com Another website Internal about.html Another page in same site Fragment #contact Section on current page Cross-page fragment about.html#team Section on another page Email mailto:test@example.com Email Telephone tel:+911234567890 Phone call Download document.pdf + download Download resource ________________ 3.27 Link Accessibility Good link text should clearly describe the destination. Good Read HTML Notes Poor Click Here Why? Descriptive link text helps: * Users understand where the link goes. * Screen-reader users navigate more easily. * Search engines understand the purpose of the link. ________________ 3.28 Links and Keyboard Accessibility Normal elements with an href are keyboard accessible. Users can generally navigate to them using the keyboard's Tab key. Example: About Us Avoid replacing normal links with non-semantic elements such as:
About Us

topics.content: 4. Images in HTML 4.1 Introduction to Images Images are used to display visual content such as: * Photos * Logos * Icons * Illustrations * Banners * Graphics * Diagrams HTML uses the element to display images. Basic Syntax Example Important Points * is a void element. * It does not have a closing tag. * src specifies the image location. * alt provides alternative text. * CSS can be used to control image size and appearance. ________________ 4.2 The src Attribute The src attribute specifies the location of the image. Example Here: src → image location alt → alternative text ________________ 4.3 Relative Image Paths A relative path points to an image relative to the current HTML file. Suppose: website/ │ ├─�� index.html └── images/ └── logo.png In index.html: ________________ 4.4 Image in the Same Folder Suppose: website/ │ ├── index.html └── logo.png Use: ________________ 4.5 Image in a Subfolder Suppose: website/ │ ├── index.html └── assets/ └── images/ └── photo.jpg Use: ________________ 4.6 Going to the Parent Folder The .. notation moves one directory upward. Suppose: website/ │ ├── index.html └── pages/ └── about.html If about.html needs to display logo.png from the parent directory: ../ means: Go up one directory. ________________ 4.7 Absolute Image URLs An image can also be loaded from another website using an absolute URL. Important Point The external server must allow the image to be accessed. ________________ 4.8 The alt Attribute The alt attribute provides alternative text for an image. Example Why alt Is Important Alternative text helps when: * The image fails to load. * A screen reader is being used. * The image cannot be visually perceived. Good alt Poor alt The alt text should describe the meaningful content or purpose of the image. ________________ 4.9 Decorative Images If an image is purely decorative and provides no meaningful information, use an empty alt attribute. This tells assistive technologies that the image can be ignored. ________________ 4.10 Images Without alt Avoid: Prefer: For decorative images: ________________ 4.11 width Attribute The width attribute specifies the rendered width of an image. The value is generally interpreted as a CSS pixel length. ________________ 4.12 height Attribute The height attribute specifies the rendered height of an image. ________________ 4.13 Using width and height Together Providing the intrinsic dimensions can help the browser reserve space for the image while the page loads. ________________ 4.14 Image Sizing with CSS For responsive images, CSS is commonly used. .responsive-image { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } This allows the image to shrink when its container becomes smaller. ________________ 4.15 Image as a Link An image can be placed inside an element. The image becomes clickable. ________________ 4.16 Image Title The title attribute can provide additional advisory information. The browser may display the title as a tooltip. Important Point Do not use title as a replacement for meaningful alt text. ________________ 4.17 Image Formats Common image formats used on websites include: Format Common Use JPEG/JPG Photographs PNG Transparency and graphics GIF Simple animations SVG Logos, icons, vector graphics WebP Efficient web images AVIF Modern high-efficiency images ________________ 4.18 JPEG / JPG JPEG is commonly used for photographs and images with many colors. Advantages * Good for photographs. * Usually smaller than uncompressed image formats. Limitation JPEG does not support transparency. ________________ 4.19 PNG PNG supports transparency and is commonly used for graphics, screenshots, and images requiring lossless compression. Common Uses * Logos * Icons * Screenshots * Transparent graphics ________________ 4.20 GIF GIF supports simple animations and limited-color images. For modern animated content, video formats may sometimes be more appropriate. ________________ 4.21 SVG SVG stands for Scalable Vector Graphics. It is useful for: * Logos * Icons * Charts * Diagrams * Vector illustrations External SVG SVG images can scale without the same pixelation associated with raster images. ________________ 4.22 WebP WebP is a modern image format designed for efficient web delivery. It can provide smaller files than older formats in many situations. ________________ 4.23 AVIF AVIF is a modern image format that can provide high compression efficiency and good image quality. Browser support should be considered when targeting older environments. ________________ 4.24 The

Web Storage API Web Storage allows websites to store data in the browser. It includes: localStorage sessionStorage localStorage Data remains stored until it is removed. localStorage.setItem("name", "Lucky"); let name = localStorage.getItem("name"); console.log(name); sessionStorage Data exists for the current browser session. sessionStorage.setItem("name", "Lucky"); let name = sessionStorage.getItem("name"); console.log(name); ________________ 4. Drag me
